headline: THE ONE THING IS DONE — the photographer is booked for tomorrow's shoot AND the seller has been told, which closes the only item on this board with a deadline inside 24 hours. · DO: call the agent whose buyers put 355 Comanche at the top of their list — she is still uncalled twelve hours later · WATCH: Make credits pause the whole automation layer around Thursday.

notes: ✅ THE ONE THING CLOSED AT MIDDAY, AND BOTH HALVES OF IT CLOSED — this board opened the day saying the 225 Willow Point shoot arrives tomorrow with no photographer booked and the sellers unanswered on day four. You ruled on it at 12:14: the photographer is booked and the seller has been told. Two chips closed on your word, and the desk deliberately reversed its own earlier advice to send the seller a written note rather than quietly dropping it — the reversal is printed in the 12:30 digest rather than buried. ⭐ The related milestone chip was HELD OPEN on purpose: the MLS prep and the never-worked buy-side half of this relationship are still live for Monday.

✅ ROUGHLY TWENTY ON-TIME PASSES SINCE MIDNIGHT, NOTHING BLOCKED, AND THE SUNDAY NO-TOUCH RULE HELD ALL MORNING — zero sends, zero drafts, zero texts by construction, which is the rule working rather than the lane being dark. The morning letter fired on time at 6:45 after a three-day slip, the midday digest sent at 12:30, and the lead lane has been genuinely dry since 10:40. ⭐ One net-new seller signal did land this morning and was caught: an owner in Indian Springs disputed the estimate on his own home at 10:26 — ownership is unverified because the CRM search was down, so it was parked for a Monday 7 AM first touch rather than guessed at.

🛑 ONE REAL COUNTDOWN AND ONE THINNING MARGIN — the automation platform is 75% through its credit cycle and every scenario on it pauses when the meter runs out, projected around Thursday, with no renewal until roughly the 30th. That is the instant-lead alert and the send path for these briefings, dark for nine days. ⚠️ Separately and new since this morning: another automatic draft posted against an account whose scheduled autos already exceed the balance sitting in it. No returned item, no NSF — this is a timing risk being tracked, not an emergency, and the figures are deliberately withheld because this page is public.

callBlock.who: Amy G. of Ethos International — her buyers put 355 Comanche TOP OF THEIR LIST, and she is still uncalled
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE HOTTEST THING ON THIS BOARD, AND IT IS NOW THIRTEEN HOURS OLD. She filed at 11:24 last night: interested — YES, and in her own words her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. ⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER YES ON THIS HOUSE: she is the same agent who phoned you from inside the home mid-showing yesterday afternoon, and you already answered half of what she asked by text. The channel is open and warm — this is a returned call, not a cold approach. ⚠️ THE HALF YOU DID NOT ANSWER IS THE PROBLEM: she reported the basement lights would not come on, and it is still open. Buyers who have 'just started looking' will tour more houses this week, and the last thing they saw in yours was a dark basement. ⏰ Sunday afternoon is when buyers who just started looking are actually out looking — the call is worth more today than tomorrow. ⭐ She also left BOTH price fields blank and scored staging a 3 — the only agent to score staging since the cut, so ask her what she would change.

callBlock.who: Robert C. — the 198 Rena buyer, and the agreement reinstates TOMORROW
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE OLDEST LIVE BUYER SIGNAL ON THE BOARD, AND THE CLOCK BEHIND IT RUNS OUT TOMORROW. He phoned you directly Thursday morning asking for photos of the workshop and the garage — not a form, a person who studied the listing closely enough to know what was missing from it. ⭐ YOUR OWN NOTE PUT A LAST NAME TO HIM AND ESCALATED WHAT HE WANTS: this stopped being a photo request and became a showing request. ⏰ THE TIMING IS NOW AS SHARP AS IT GETS — the listing agreement reinstates TOMORROW, so a buyer asking to walk through arrives in the same twenty-four hours the sellers decide whether to keep going. On a listing that produced one written offer all summer, an unrepresented buyer asking to see it is the cheapest at-bat you own, and it is the single strongest argument for reinstating. ⚠️ Stated honestly: if you called him from the truck it would not show here.

The document still sitting in the drafts folder is a DUPLICATE created six minutes later, and it is flagged for deletion rather than aging as pending follow-up. Two separate reads called it 'unsent for 24 hours'; both were reading the copy, not the original. ⭐ THE SHAPE OF THE ASK IS THE STORY AND IT IS GOOD NEWS: they inspected seventy-one items, flagged sixty-eight at some level, and then asked for exactly three. That is a reasonable buyer. ⭐ THE RECOMMENDATION YOU SENT IS TWO YESES AND A HOLD — agree to the basement leak and to a scoped HVAC service, and on the roof do not say no, say give us a few days and our own licensed roofer's report. The inspector wrote in the same section that he cannot determine the roof's age or remaining life, which is the report itself saying the roof question is unanswered. ⚠️ TWO THINGS BEFORE FIGHTING THE ROOF: this is FHA, so the appraiser can raise it independently, and the concession room left under the FHA cap is small, so this gets solved with work rather than a check. ✅ The sellers have acknowledged the roof-holdback approach. ⭐ Closing 10/23 — roughly ten weeks, which is a luxury most files do not get.

She wrote. Offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes. Patience was the right call. ⭐ Closing 9/14.
